# General arrow constructor study

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

Five complete first sources retain sequence, ordered tensor, a two-sided
unitor adjoint, a differing-tree pair with an endomorphic result and a
wrong-middle-tree counterexample. Actual pre-change observations are preserved
in [session.json](session.json); no baseline refusal is a proof of the desired
semantics. Independent small exact/complex checks must follow implementation.

The appended native observations check the unchanged five source snapshots:
all four intended positives now reach fresh hierarchy acceptance and the wrong
middle tree still rejects. `tests/general_operation_arrows.rs` independently
specifies small complex amplitudes for those programs, non-real phase,
endomorphic powers, ordered pure tensor, packed control and conjugation order.
The initialization replay tests additionally reject omitted/reordered tensor
boundaries, a wrong constructor path, a changed structural node and reversed
returned axes. These observations do not prove general source preservation.

Constructor subtrees are immutable and shared; expanded traversal is charged
against the existing specialization cell budget before copying or key creation.
A small source with repeated binary forwarding checks rejection at that budget;
it generates no large fixture or maximum-qubit program. Raw constructor
materialization and attached constructor Meanings remain explicit unsupported
profiles. Zero powers retain those child obligations. No Issue is completed by
this bounded study, and the broader #83/#46 and QS/PR/RS obligations remain.

The constructor sequence additionally matches the existing independently
written exact Unit-elimination/H equation. A native-valid X substitution fails
that independent request, although initialization-movement checking alone
accepts it. This test makes the two verification scopes explicit; a producer's
own comparison request does not establish the source's intended gate action.

Three additional curated counterexamples in `attempt-02` were first checked
under a temporary directory during review; their byte-identical sources,
original commands, hashes and raw successful outputs are retained. They are
additional probes, not repairs to the five first sources. After correction,
the unused non-endomorphic runtime adjoint rejects with `type`, and powers
outside constructed sequences or adjoints retain the existing repetition
product limit of 256. All three unchanged probes now reject. The regression
also covers tensor, controlled and conjugate constructors and checks that
the corresponding products exactly at 256 remain supported. These are host
checking bounds and source type checks, not quantitative RS discharge.
